survey: A spiral water slide beside a pool, seen in three-quarter view from the front left. A square yellow platform sits on a central blue pole, braced to its underside by two diagonal struts. A yellow railing with ball-topped posts runs along the back and right edges of the deck, and its posts stand on the deck. A blue ladder leans against the platform's right side: its two feet rest on the tiles, its rungs span both rails, and its rails loop over at the top to land on the deck. The green open chute leaves the platform's back-left corner and swings left, then right in front of the central pole, then left again, and runs down to the pool edge. A second, shorter blue pole stands on the tiles and rises behind the lower turn to hold it up. The slide's exit lies on the pool coping, and a stream of water pours from it into the pool. The tool marks are all on the railing and the ladder top. Each end mark lands on a post, the deck or a ladder rail, and each branch is a real rail-to-post joint, so there are no loose ends.

errors.where: Top of the slide, where the green chute meets the yellow platform (upper left of the deck)
errors.what: The chute's upper end slides behind the platform's front edge. No entry opening or joint between deck and chute can be seen, so it is unclear where a rider would get onto the slide. It looks tucked behind the deck rather than built onto it.

errors.where: Slide exit at the pool edge (bottom left)
errors.what: A heavy stream of water gushes out of the slide's exit, but the chute above it is dry along its whole length. Nothing feeds the water at the top, so the flow seems to start from nowhere at the end of the slide.

fix: Show the top of the green slide fixed to the left edge of the yellow platform, with a clear open entry flush with the deck where a rider would sit down. Show a thin film of water running down the whole chute from the top, ending in the small splash at the pool exit.
